University of British Columbia Professors Sue School Over Political Correctness
Pranav BaskarIs it political to say that land was never given up by Indigenous people? What about asking job applicants to commit to diversity? A group of Canadian professors thinks so.

Pranav BaskarThey are suing one of the country’s top universities, saying it’s broken a law mandating that universities stay out of politics in a case that’s currently under review by the Supreme Court of British Columbia.
Pranav BaskarThe professors argue that when the university requires commitments to D.E.I., for example, it endorses a political mold and stifles freedom of thought on campus.
Pranav BaskarBut their opponents call it a contrived effort to undermine diversity efforts. They say forcing neutrality on contentious matters is just as political of a move.

Pranav BaskarThe case reflects how Trump-era opposition to social justice efforts is spreading north to Canada. But it also raises a bigger question: In an era of polarization, what counts as political?
